name: John McCarthy
bio: John McCarthy coined the term "artificial intelligence" in the 1955 proposal for the Dartmouth summer workshop, the event usually treated as the founding of the field. He invented the Lisp programming language and founded the Stanford AI Lab. He believed human-level AI was achievable in principle and spent decades on common-sense reasoning. In 1973 he defended AI research against the Lighthill report in a televised debate.

name: Miles Brundage
org: Formerly OpenAI (Head of Policy Research, AGI Readiness)
bio: Miles Brundage spent six years at OpenAI leading policy research and AGI readiness work. He left in 2024 to work independently on AI policy.
warning: No frontier lab is ready for AGI, and neither is the world.

quotes.text: In short, neither OpenAI nor any other frontier lab is ready, and the world is also not ready.
quotes.source: Why I'm leaving OpenAI and what I'm doing next (Substack)

name: Romeo Dean
bio: Romeo Dean is a researcher at the AI Futures Project who forecasts AI chip production and use and works on compute governance.

name: Will MacAskill
bio: Will MacAskill is a Scottish philosopher and one of the founders of effective altruism. At Forethought he studies how to prepare society for an intelligence explosion.
warning: AI could squeeze a century of progress into a few years, and we are not ready for the challenges.

quotes.text: AI that can accelerate research could drive a century of technological progress over just a few years.
quotes.source: Preparing for the Intelligence Explosion (with Fin Moorhouse)

name: Will MacAskill
role: Senior research fellow; co-founder of effective altruism
bio: Will MacAskill is a philosopher who co-founded the effective altruism movement and wrote 'What We Owe the Future'. At Forethought he now researches how society could navigate an intelligence explosion.
key_ideas: Co-founder of effective altruism, Giving What We Can and 80,000 Hours
Author of 'What We Owe the Future' (2022)
Research on 'Preparing for the Intelligence Explosion'

name: Alex Turner
bio: Alex Turner, known online as TurnTrout, works on AI alignment. He developed a formal theory of power-seeking tendencies in AI agents and worked on shard theory and steering vectors.

name: Anthony Aguirre
bio: Anthony Aguirre is a cosmologist and the co-founder and CEO of the Future of Life Institute. He also co-founded the forecasting site Metaculus in 2015.

name: Brian Christian
bio: Brian Christian is an author who writes about what computer science means for people. His book The Alignment Problem explains AI alignment in plain words.

name: Christopher Summerfield
role: Research Director; Professor of Cognitive Neuroscience
org: UK AI Security Institute / University of Oxford
bio: Christopher Summerfield is a professor of cognitive neuroscience at Oxford and research director at the UK AI Security Institute. He wrote 'These Strange New Minds' about how language models work.

name: Dylan Hadfield-Menell
bio: Dylan Hadfield-Menell runs the Algorithmic Alignment Group at MIT CSAIL. His group works on making AI behave in line with the goals of users and society.

name: Ethan Perez
bio: Ethan Perez leads an alignment team at Anthropic. He works on red teaming language models and finding their failures with model-written evaluations.
warning: He signed Pacing the Frontier, warning that safety teams have to sprint to stop new risks every few months and will soon hit problems that need more time.

quotes.text: With the current rate of AI progress, safety teams at AI companies have to sprint to prevent new risks to society every few months. At some point, we’re going to hit problems we need more time to solve.
quotes.source: Pacing the Frontier, signatory comment

name: Jürgen Schmidhuber
bio: Jürgen Schmidhuber's lab co-invented the LSTM neural network, which powered speech recognition and translation for years before transformers. He proposed self-improving "Gödel machines" and theories of artificial curiosity as early as the 1990s. He predicts that AIs will eventually far surpass humans and spread through the cosmos, but argues this need not be feared. He is a prominent counter-voice to AI doom warnings.

quotes.text: Don’t think of humans as the crown of creation.
quotes.source: Interview in Forbes (via Wikiquote)

name: Lennart Heim
bio: Lennart Heim researches compute governance, the idea of using control over AI chips and data centers as a lever for safety. He co-wrote Epoch AI's influential study of training compute trends.
warning: Compute is growing fast and is one of the few parts of AI that governments can measure and control.

quotes.text: Furthermore, we find that the training compute has grown by a factor of 10 billion since 2010, with a doubling rate of around 5-6 months.
quotes.source: Compute Trends Across Three Eras of Machine Learning (co-author, Epoch AI)

name: Andrea Miotti
bio: Andrea Miotti is the founder and CEO of ControlAI, a nonprofit campaigning in the UK, US and other countries for a ban on developing superintelligence. A former policy professional, he co-authored the policy plan 'A Narrow Path'.
key_ideas: Founded ControlAI and its campaign that has signed up 100+ UK lawmakers on superintelligence risk
Co-author of 'A Narrow Path', a policy blueprint for safe transformative AI
Testified to the Canadian House of Commons on extinction risk from AI

name: Beth Barnes
bio: Beth Barnes founded METR, a nonprofit that tests frontier AI models for dangerous abilities before and after release. She worked at OpenAI before starting METR.
warning: The world should not be taken by surprise by dangerous AI, so we need real tests before it arrives.

quotes.text: They are, in some sense, these vast alien intelligences,
quotes.source: Interview with TIME

quotes.text: Yeah, so basically, the basic mission is: have the world not be taken by surprise by dangerous AI stuff happening.
quotes.source: AXRP podcast episode 34

name: Carl Shulman
bio: Carl Shulman is an independent researcher, formerly at the Future of Humanity Institute, known for detailed thinking about the intelligence explosion, AI takeover and the economics of a world after AGI. He rarely gives interviews, but his long conversations are highly influential.
key_ideas: Detailed models of the intelligence explosion and robot economies
Influential analysis of AI takeover scenarios
Advised Open Philanthropy on AI risk

name: Daniel Dennett
bio: Daniel Dennett argued that consciousness is not a mysterious inner light but a 'user illusion' produced by many parallel brain processes, which in principle means machines could be conscious too; in the 1990s he helped MIT's Cog humanoid-robot project. In From Bacteria to Bach and Back (2017) he said superintelligence was at least 50 years away and less urgent than other problems. His real worry was that people would over-trust 'parasitic' AI systems and credit them with understanding they lack. In 2023 he called AI-generated 'counterfeit people' one of the most dangerous artifacts in history and urged that companies making them be held liable.
key_ideas: Consciousness as a 'user illusion' / Multiple Drafts model
Strong AI possible in principle but far harder than feared
Danger of 'counterfeit people' and over-trusting AI
stance: AI as tools, not colleagues; ban counterfeit people

quotes.text: Consciousness is the biggest mystery. It may be the largest outstanding obstacle in our quest for a scientific understanding of the universe.
quotes.source: The Conscious Mind: In Search of a Fundamental Theory (via Wikiquote)

quotes.text: It could be a disaster to stumble upon AI consciousness unknowingly and unreflectively.
quotes.source: Could a Large Language Model Be Conscious?, Boston Review

name: David Chalmers
role: Philosopher of mind; co-director, NYU Center for Mind, Brain and Consciousness
bio: David Chalmers named the 'hard problem of consciousness' in 1995: why physical processing is accompanied by subjective experience at all. His 'fading qualia' thought experiment argues that a brain whose neurons are gradually replaced by functionally identical chips would stay conscious, so he holds that silicon can in principle be as conscious as carbon. In 2010 he wrote one of the first serious philosophical analyses of the intelligence explosion and the Singularity. In his 2022 NeurIPS talk he put the chance that current LLMs are conscious at under 10 percent, but said serious candidates for machine consciousness could arrive within a decade.
key_ideas: Organisational invariance: silicon minds can be conscious
Conscious LLM+ systems may be a serious possibility within a decade
stance: AI consciousness is possible and may come soon; proceed reflectively

name: Fei-Fei Li
bio: Fei-Fei Li created ImageNet, the huge labelled image dataset whose 2012 contest launched the deep-learning boom. She co-directs Stanford's Institute for Human-Centered AI and argues AI should augment people rather than replace them. She co-founded World Labs to build AI with "spatial intelligence" that understands the 3D world. She is often called the "godmother of AI".

quotes.text: I believe in human-centered AI to benefit people in positive and benevolent ways.
quotes.source: Quoted in The New York Times (via Wikipedia)

books: The Worlds I See: Curiosity, Exploration, and Discovery at the Dawn of AI

name: Holden Karnofsky
org: Co-founder of GiveWell and Open Philanthropy
bio: Holden Karnofsky co-founded GiveWell and Open Philanthropy, one of the biggest funders of AI safety. His Cold Takes blog argues this could be the most important century in history.
warning: Advanced AI could defeat all of humanity combined if it were pointed toward that goal.

quotes.text: As a first step, this post will emphasize an unoriginal but extremely important point: the kind of AI I've discussed could defeat all of humanity combined, if (for whatever reason) it were pointed toward that goal.
quotes.source: AI Could Defeat All Of Us Combined (Cold Takes)

quotes.text: I've become convinced that humanity as a whole faces huge risks and opportunities this century.
quotes.source: The Most Important Century series (Cold Takes)

name: Ian Goodfellow
bio: Ian Goodfellow invented generative adversarial networks, or GANs. He was the first author of the textbook Deep Learning.

name: Jaime Sevilla
bio: Jaime Sevilla leads Epoch AI, which tracks the data behind AI progress, such as how much computing power models use. Epoch's charts are used by labs, governments and journalists.
warning: The compute used to train AI is growing extremely fast, and we need good data to see where it leads.

quotes.text: Furthermore, we find that the training compute has grown by a factor of 10 billion since 2010, with a doubling rate of around 5-6 months.
quotes.source: Compute Trends Across Three Eras of Machine Learning (lead author, Epoch AI)

name: Liv Boeree
bio: Liv Boeree is a former world-champion poker player and science communicator who hosts the Win-Win podcast. She popularised the idea of 'Moloch' – destructive competitive races – and applies it to the AI race.
key_ideas: World Series of Poker and European Poker Tour champion
Popularised 'Moloch' as a frame for harmful competition, including in AI
TED talk 'The Dark Side of Competition in AI'

name: Markus Anderljung
org: Centre for the Governance of AI (GovAI)
bio: Markus Anderljung is a policy researcher at GovAI. He was lead author of 'Frontier AI Regulation', which helped shape how governments talk about frontier models.
warning: The most capable AI models need their own rules because their dangers can appear without warning.

quotes.text: In this paper, we focus on what we term "frontier AI"
quotes.source: Frontier AI Regulation: Managing Emerging Risks to Public Safety (lead author), arXiv

name: Robin Hanson
bio: Robin Hanson is an economist at George Mason University known for prediction markets. He was a research associate at Oxford's Future of Humanity Institute.

name: Steven Adler
bio: Steven Adler is a former OpenAI safety researcher. He now writes Clear-Eyed AI about how to avoid the worst risks of powerful AI.
warning: He argues OpenAI chose its nonprofit limits on purpose and should not be allowed to drop them now.

quotes.text: OpenAI voluntarily chose to start as a nonprofit and to take on various constraints, in return for garnering various related advantages; it shouldn't now get to renege on those constraints.
quotes.source: Post on X, via The OpenAI Files

name: Vincent Conitzer
role: Professor of Computer Science; director of the FOCAL lab
org: Carnegie Mellon University; University of Oxford
bio: Vincent Conitzer is a computer scientist working at the meeting point of AI, game theory and ethics. He directs CMU's Foundations of Cooperative AI Lab and studies how AI agents that can be copied and simulated should cooperate, and how social choice can guide AI alignment.
key_ideas: Director of the Foundations of Cooperative AI Lab (FOCAL) at CMU
Computational social choice and mechanism design
Work on moral AI and social choice for alignment

name: Arvind Narayanan
bio: Arvind Narayanan directs Princeton's Center for Information Technology Policy and co-wrote AI Snake Oil. With Sayash Kapoor he wrote 'AI as Normal Technology' (2025).
warning: AI is a normal, powerful technology that society can adapt to, not an impending superintelligence.

quotes.text: AI as normal technology is a worldview that stands in contrast to the worldview of AI as impending superintelligence.
quotes.source: AI as Normal Technology (with Sayash Kapoor)

name: Daniel Murfet
bio: Daniel Murfet is a mathematician who moved from algebraic geometry into AI safety and leads the learning-theory side of Timaeus (now Resolution). He is a leading advocate of singular learning theory for alignment.
key_ideas: Singular learning theory for AI safety

name: Dawn Song
bio: Dawn Song is a computer security expert and a professor at UC Berkeley. She won a MacArthur Fellowship in 2010.
warning: She signed Pacing the Frontier, warning that AI progress may move faster than society is ready for.

quotes.text: Frontier AI capabilities are advancing rapidly, and the pace of progress is itself accelerating. We see this directly in our evaluation work.
quotes.source: Pacing the Frontier, signatory comment

name: Eric Ho
bio: Eric Ho is co-founder and CEO of Goodfire, which builds tools to understand and edit the internals of neural networks. He previously founded the recruiting startup RippleMatch.
key_ideas: Public advocacy for understanding AI internals

name: Geoffrey Irving
org: UK AI Security Institute (formerly OpenAI, Google DeepMind)
bio: Geoffrey Irving works on scalable oversight, the problem of supervising AI that is smarter than us. He proposed 'AI safety via debate' and has worked at OpenAI, Google DeepMind and the UK AI Security Institute.
warning: To supervise AI smarter than us, we may need AIs to debate each other while humans judge.

quotes.text: To help address this concern, we propose training agents via self play on a zero sum debate game.
quotes.source: AI safety via debate (lead author), arXiv

name: Jacob Hilton
bio: Jacob Hilton is a researcher at the Alignment Research Center and worked at OpenAI before that. In 2024 he signed the 'A Right to Warn' letter asking AI companies to protect whistleblowers.
warning: People inside AI labs must be able to warn the public about serious risks.

quotes.text: These risks range from the further entrenchment of existing inequalities, to manipulation and misinformation, to the loss of control of autonomous AI systems potentially resulting in human extinction.
quotes.source: A Right to Warn about Advanced AI (open letter, signatory)

name: Rosie Campbell
bio: Rosie Campbell is the managing director of Eleos AI Research, which studies the possible wellbeing of AI systems. Before that she led the Policy Frontiers team at OpenAI.
warning: She left OpenAI saying she was unsettled by shifts at the company and the loss of people who shaped its safety culture.

quotes.text: I’ve been unsettled by some of the shifts over the last ~year, and the loss of so many people who shaped our culture.
quotes.source: Leaving OpenAI (blog post)

name: Sean O hEigeartaigh
org: Leverhulme Centre for the Future of Intelligence, Cambridge
bio: Sean O hEigeartaigh is associate director for research strategy at the Leverhulme Centre for the Future of Intelligence in Cambridge, where he directs the AI: Futures and Responsibility programme.

name: Steven Byrnes
bio: Steven Byrnes is an AGI safety researcher at the Astera Institute with a physics PhD from UC Berkeley. He studies how a brain-like AGI could be made safe, drawing on neuroscience of social instincts.
key_ideas: Learning vs steering subsystems model of the brain

name: Vanessa Kosoy
bio: Vanessa Kosoy is a theoretical alignment researcher. She is research lead at CORAL and director of AI research at ALTER, and does her PhD at the Technion.

name: Yuval Noah Harari
bio: Yuval Noah Harari is a historian and the author of Sapiens. His book Nexus looks at how AI could change who holds power over information.

name: Zvi Mowshowitz
bio: Zvi Mowshowitz writes 'Don't Worry About the Vase', a widely read weekly analysis of AI developments with a focus on safety and policy. A former professional Magic: The Gathering player and trader, he is known for detailed, sceptical takes on lab claims.
key_ideas: Weekly AI roundups on his Substack, read across the AI industry
Detailed critiques of AI lab safety policies and model releases
Former Magic: The Gathering pro and game designer

name: Aaron Roth
role: Professor of Computer and Information Science
bio: Aaron Roth is a computer science professor at Penn known for work on differential privacy, algorithmic fairness and calibration. In 2026 he taught and published a full lecture course, 'Mathematical Foundations of AI Alignment'.
key_ideas: Co-author of 'The Algorithmic Foundations of Differential Privacy' and 'The Ethical Algorithm'
Public lecture series on the mathematics of AI alignment (debate, delegation, social choice)

name: Blake Richards
role: Neuroscientist and AI researcher; Associate Professor
org: Mila – Quebec AI Institute; McGill University
bio: Blake Richards studies how the brain could learn in ways similar to deep learning, including biologically plausible versions of backpropagation. He argues that deep learning offers a useful framework for neuroscience and that the brain and AI may share universal principles of intelligence. On safety, he has publicly pushed back against existential-risk framing, arguing that 'general intelligence' is not a single dial and that near-term harms deserve more attention than speculative takeover scenarios. He is a CIFAR fellow and co-organiser of NeuroAI meetings.
key_ideas: Deep learning as a framework for understanding the brain
Biologically plausible credit assignment in cortex
Sceptical of AI x-risk framing; focus on concrete harms

name: Gillian Hadfield
role: Bloomberg Distinguished Professor of AI Alignment and Governance
bio: Gillian Hadfield is an economist and legal scholar who works on AI alignment and governance. She was a senior policy adviser to OpenAI from 2018 to 2023.

name: Jack Lindsey
bio: Jack Lindsey leads model psychology research at Anthropic, part of its work on understanding what happens inside language models.

name: Josh Batson
bio: Josh Batson is a research scientist on Anthropic's interpretability team and a former mathematician and computational biologist. He was a lead on the 'Biology of a Large Language Model' circuit-tracing work.
key_ideas: Scaling dictionary learning to Claude 3 Sonnet
Explains interpretability as moving 'from art towards science'

name: Karl Friston
role: Theoretical neuroscientist; architect of the free energy principle
org: University College London; VERSES AI (chief scientist)
bio: Karl Friston is one of the most cited neuroscientists alive, known for brain-imaging methods and for the free energy principle: the idea that any living system survives by minimising surprise about its world. Its offshoot, active inference, treats perception, action and learning as one process of a self-modelling agent, and Friston argues this is a better foundation for intelligent machines than today's large models. He pictures future AI as networks of many small, curious agents that share beliefs, rather than one giant system. He works with the company VERSES on building such systems.
key_ideas: Free energy principle: minimise surprise to stay alive
Active inference unifies perception, action and learning
stance: Active inference, not scaling, as the route to real AI

name: Kate Crawford
bio: Kate Crawford studies the social and political side of AI. She co-founded the AI Now Institute and wrote Atlas of AI in 2021.

name: Kimberly Stachenfeld
bio: Kim Stachenfeld is best known for 'The hippocampus as a predictive map' (2017, with Matthew Botvinick and Samuel Gershman), which proposed that the hippocampus stores predictions about where an animal will go next, using the successor representation from reinforcement learning. At DeepMind she works on predictive models of memory, learning and physical simulation that serve both AI and neuroscience. Her work is a leading example of how ideas move back and forth between brains and AI systems. More recently she has explored using large language models to discover symbolic models of cognition.
warning: She signed Pacing the Frontier to support international cooperation on AI and to understand technology used at massive scale.

quotes.text: I am signing because I support efforts to build international cooperation around AI, and believe it's important to understand the consequences of technology we are applying at massive scale in potentially high stakes contexts.
quotes.source: Pacing the Frontier, signatory comment

key_ideas: Hippocampus as a predictive map (successor representation)
Structured predictive models for brains and machines
LLMs as tools to discover cognitive models

name: Lisa Feldman Barrett
role: Distinguished Professor of Psychology; affective scientist
bio: Lisa Feldman Barrett's theory of constructed emotion says the brain does not detect emotions but predicts and builds them from bodily signals and past experience. Her central idea is that the brain's main job is to regulate the body's energy budget, with thinking and feeling built on top of that. This makes her critical of 'emotion AI' that claims to read feelings from faces, which she argues rests on a scientific myth. Her work supports the view that human intelligence is deeply tied to having a body, which current AI lacks.
key_ideas: The predicting brain runs a 'body budget' (allostasis)
stance: Critic of emotion-reading AI; intelligence is embodied

name: Malo Bourgon
bio: Malo Bourgon is the chief executive officer of the Machine Intelligence Research Institute (MIRI), the group co-founded by Eliezer Yudkowsky.

name: Marcus Hutter
bio: Marcus Hutter developed AIXI, a mathematical definition of a perfectly intelligent agent that learns and acts optimally in any computable environment. His book Universal Artificial Intelligence (2005) gave AGI and superintelligence a formal theoretical foundation. He also created the Hutter Prize, which rewards compressing human knowledge as a stand-in for intelligence. More recently he has applied the AIXI framework to the safety of superintelligent systems.

name: Matthew Botvinick
role: Cognitive neuroscientist; former Director of Neuroscience Research at DeepMind
bio: Matt Botvinick led DeepMind's neuroscience research, studying how ideas from deep reinforcement learning shed light on the brain and vice versa. His team showed links between dopamine signals and distributional reinforcement learning, and proposed that the prefrontal cortex works as a 'meta-learning' system that learns how to learn. He sees AI as a window onto human intelligence and has more recently turned to how AI will affect society and democracy.
key_ideas: Meta-learning in prefrontal cortex and in AI
AI as a window on human intelligence
stance: Neuroscience and AI should inform each other; mindful of societal impact

name: Michael Graziano
role: Professor of Psychology and Neuroscience; novelist
bio: Michael Graziano's Attention Schema Theory says the brain builds a simplified model of its own attention, and that this model is what we describe as conscious awareness. Because the theory is mechanistic, he argues there is nothing in principle stopping machines from being built with the same kind of self-model. He goes further, suggesting that giving AI an attention schema, and with it a model of other minds, could make it more cooperative and therefore safer. His ideas are being tested in AI systems through the Astound project.
key_ideas: Machine consciousness is buildable in principle
Conscious, socially aware AI might be safer
stance: Conscious AI is coming and could be safer

name: Pushmeet Kohli
role: VP of Research, Science and Strategic Initiatives
bio: Pushmeet Kohli is an Indian British computer scientist and vice president of research at Google DeepMind. He has led projects like AlphaFold, AlphaEvolve and the SynthID watermark.

name: Sam Bowman
bio: Sam Bowman is a language model researcher at Anthropic and a professor at NYU. His 2023 paper 'Eight Things to Know about Large Language Models' became a popular primer.
warning: We do not yet have reliable ways to steer or understand large language models.

quotes.text: There are no reliable techniques for steering the behavior of LLMs.
quotes.source: Eight Things to Know about Large Language Models, arXiv

quotes.text: Experts are not yet able to interpret the inner workings of LLMs.
quotes.source: Eight Things to Know about Large Language Models, arXiv

name: Terrence Sejnowski
bio: Terry Sejnowski co-invented the Boltzmann machine with Geoffrey Hinton in the 1980s and helped found the field of neural networks, as well as the NeurIPS conference foundation. His books The Deep Learning Revolution (2018) and ChatGPT and the Future of AI (2024) tell how brain-inspired ideas led to modern AI. He argues that large language models act like a mirror of their users, and that neuroscience and AI will keep borrowing from each other. He tends to be optimistic, treating AI as a powerful tool to understand both brains and ourselves.
key_ideas: Boltzmann machine (with Hinton) and early neural networks
Brain and AI research as a two-way street
LLMs as a 'mirror' reflecting the user's intelligence

name: William Saunders
bio: William Saunders worked on OpenAI's Superalignment team and resigned in 2024. He signed the 'A Right to Warn' letter and later spoke to the US Senate about safety at AI labs.
warning: Insiders must be free to warn the public when AI companies take serious risks.

quotes.text: These risks range from the further entrenchment of existing inequalities, to manipulation and misinformation, to the loss of control of autonomous AI systems potentially resulting in human extinction.
quotes.source: A Right to Warn about Advanced AI (open letter, signatory)

name: Abeba Birhane
bio: Abeba Birhane is an Ethiopian-born cognitive scientist who studies bias in AI. With Vinay Prabhu she found racist and misogynistic labels in big image datasets like 80 Million Tiny Images.
warning: Her work shows that the data used to train AI can carry harmful bias that hurts people, often those with the least power.

name: Abram Demski
bio: Abram Demski is an agent foundations researcher, formerly at MIRI, known for work on decision theory, logical uncertainty and embedded agency. He co-wrote the 'Embedded Agency' sequence with Scott Garrabrant.

name: Akiko Murakami
bio: Akiko Murakami has led the Japan AI Safety Institute since it opened in February 2024. She is also group chief data officer at Sompo Holdings.

name: Alondra Nelson
bio: Alondra Nelson is a sociologist and policy adviser. She helped lead science policy at the White House, including a Bill of Rights for automated technologies, and sat on the UN advisory body on AI.

name: Amit Sheth
role: Founding Director, AI Institute of South Carolina
bio: Amit Sheth is an Indian computer scientist and the founding director of the AI Institute of South Carolina. He is known for work on semantics and knowledge-based AI.

name: Andrej Karpathy
bio: Andrej Karpathy was a founding member of OpenAI and led Tesla's Autopilot vision team. He is one of the best-known explainers of how neural networks and large language models work, through free courses and long talks. He coined the term "vibe coding" in 2025 and argued AGI is still about a decade away. In 2026 he joined Anthropic to lead a pretraining research team.
key_ideas: "Software 2.0" and LLMs as a new computer
teaching AI from scratch (Zero to Hero)

name: Antonio Damasio
role: Neuroscientist; director of the Brain and Creativity Institute
bio: Antonio Damasio showed, in Descartes' Error (1994) and later books, that emotions and bodily feelings are essential to reasoning, not obstacles to it. He argues that consciousness grows out of homeostasis, the body's constant work to keep itself alive, and the feelings that report on it. From this he concludes that AI can sound conscious while feeling nothing, because it has no vulnerable body to regulate. He has suggested that machines with something like homeostasis and 'vulnerability' would be a different and more brain-like kind of AI.
key_ideas: Somatic marker hypothesis: emotion guides reason
Feelings and homeostasis as the roots of consciousness
AI without a vulnerable body has no real feelings
stance: AI can mimic minds but lacks feeling without a body

name: Balaraman Ravindran
role: Professor of Data Science and AI
org: Wadhwani School of Data Science and AI, IIT Madras
bio: Balaraman Ravindran is a professor at IIT Madras who works on reinforcement learning and responsible AI. He is an author of the International AI Safety Report.

name: Ben Garfinkel
org: Centre for the Governance of AI (GovAI)
bio: Ben Garfinkel is the director of the Centre for the Governance of AI and a former research fellow at Oxford's Future of Humanity Institute. He is known for carefully scrutinising the classic arguments for AI existential risk.
key_ideas: 'How sure are we about this AI stuff?' – an influential sceptical review of AI risk arguments
Directs GovAI, a leading AI governance research organisation
Research on AI, democracy and the long-run impact of technology

name: Ben Shneiderman
bio: Ben Shneiderman is a pioneer of human-computer interaction at the University of Maryland. He developed ideas like direct manipulation and his eight rules of interface design.

name: Benjamin Mann
bio: Benjamin Mann is a co-founder of Anthropic. He was an author on the GPT-3 paper at OpenAI before leaving to help start Anthropic.

name: Benjamin Rosman
bio: Benjamin Rosman is a professor at the University of the Witwatersrand in South Africa who works on robot learning and responsible AI.

name: Bernhard Scholkopf
org: Max Planck Institute for Intelligent Systems
bio: Bernhard Scholkopf is a German computer scientist known for kernel methods and causal machine learning. He directs a department at the Max Planck Institute for Intelligent Systems in Tubingen and chairs ELLIS.

name: Catherine Olsson
bio: Catherine Olsson is a researcher at Anthropic. She was first author of In-context Learning and Induction Heads, an early mechanistic interpretability paper.

name: Chris Painter
bio: Chris Painter is president of METR, the nonprofit that studies whether the most advanced AI agents are on track to escape their developers' control.

name: David Duvenaud
bio: David Duvenaud is a Canadian computer scientist at the University of Toronto who moved into AI safety in 2023. At Anthropic he led the Alignment Evaluations team.
warning: He warns of gradual disempowerment: as AI gets more capable, the systems people depend on may stop needing or serving humans.

name: Dean W. Ball
bio: Dean Ball is an AI policy researcher. He was the main author of the 2025 US AI Action Plan at the White House.

name: Emmanuel Ameisen
bio: Emmanuel Ameisen is an interpretability researcher at Anthropic and author of 'Building Machine Learning Powered Applications'. He co-led Anthropic's circuit-tracing methods paper.
key_ideas: Co-lead of 'Circuit Tracing: Revealing Computational Graphs in Language Models'
Explains how models plan ahead and hallucinate
Previously led applied ML at Stripe and Insight

name: Emmett Shear
bio: Emmett Shear co-founded Justin.tv and ran Twitch until 2023. He was briefly interim CEO of OpenAI in November 2023 and now runs the alignment startup Softmax.

name: Esben Kran
bio: Esben Kran is a board member of Apart Research, a nonprofit that runs AI safety research sprints and fellowships open to anyone.

name: Fernanda Viegas
bio: Fernanda Viegas is a Brazilian computer scientist and designer who works on data visualization. With Martin Wattenberg she co-led Google's Big Picture data visualization group.

name: Florian Tramer
bio: Florian Tramer is an assistant professor at ETH Zurich, where he leads the SPY Lab. He studies the worst-case behavior of large language models to protect user safety and privacy.

name: Giulio Tononi
role: Neuroscientist and psychiatrist; Distinguished Chair in Consciousness Science
bio: Giulio Tononi proposed Integrated Information Theory (IIT) in 2004, a mathematical theory that measures consciousness as integrated information, called Φ (phi). IIT says experience depends on a system's physical cause-and-effect structure, so a feed-forward network or a standard digital computer could behave intelligently while having almost no consciousness. This gives IIT sharp and controversial predictions about AI: copying a brain's behaviour in software would not copy its experience. IIT is one of the main theories now used in debates about whether AI could ever be conscious.
key_ideas: Consciousness depends on physical causal structure
Behavioural copies of brains need not be conscious
stance: Conventional computers are not conscious, whatever their intelligence

name: Hiroaki Kitano
bio: Hiroaki Kitano is a Japanese scientist and the CTO of Sony Group. He is known for the AIBO robot dog and for starting the RoboCup robot soccer tournament.

name: Holger Hoos
role: Alexander von Humboldt Professor of AI
bio: Holger Hoos is a German-Canadian computer scientist and Humboldt professor of AI at RWTH Aachen. He works on automated algorithm design and machine learning.

name: Jascha Sohl-Dickstein
bio: Jascha Sohl-Dickstein is best known for inventing diffusion models, which power many image generators. He now works at Anthropic.

name: Jasjeet Sekhon
bio: Jasjeet Sekhon is a statistician and political scientist known for work on causal inference and machine learning. He is chief strategy officer at Google DeepMind.
warning: He signed Pacing the Frontier and says we must build tools to pace the riskiest capabilities before we need them.

quotes.text: We can capture the benefits of the coming intelligence explosion while managing its risks, but only if we build the tools to pace the frontier of the riskiest capabilities before we need them, so we protect people and keep the social trust that innovation depends on. I believe smart technical and governance tools will be needed to sustain rapid innovation, vigorous competition, and robust safety.
quotes.source: Pacing the Frontier, signatory comment

name: Jeff Dean
bio: Jeff Dean is a computer scientist who joined Google in 1999 and helped build its large computer systems. He led Google AI from 2018 to 2023 and was Google's chief scientist until 2026.

name: Jerry Tworek
bio: Jerry Tworek is CEO of Core Automation. At OpenAI he was the second author on the Codex paper.

name: Jonas Geiping
org: ELLIS Institute and MPI for Intelligent Systems, Tubingen
bio: Jonas Geiping leads a research group on safety and efficiency aligned learning in Tubingen. He studies how to build safe intelligent systems.

name: Kai-Fu Lee
bio: Kai-Fu Lee is a computer scientist and investor. He founded Microsoft Research Asia, ran Google China, and wrote AI Superpowers.

name: Luke Muehlhauser
bio: Luke Muehlhauser leads AI governance grantmaking at Open Philanthropy and was previously executive director of the Machine Intelligence Research Institute (then the Singularity Institute). He has worked on AI risk strategy for over a decade.
key_ideas: Executive Director of MIRI / Singularity Institute (2011–2015)
Leads AI governance and policy grantmaking at Open Philanthropy

name: Marc Andreessen
bio: Marc Andreessen co-created the Mosaic web browser and co-founded the venture firm Andreessen Horowitz. His 2023 essay Why AI Will Save the World is a leading optimist case.
warning: AI will not destroy the world and may save it, because it has no goals of its own.

quotes.text: Fortunately, I am here to bring the good news: AI will not destroy the world, and in fact may save it.
quotes.source: Why AI Will Save the World (essay)

quotes.text: In short, AI doesn’t want, it doesn’t have goals, it doesn’t want to kill you, because it’s not alive.
quotes.source: Why AI Will Save the World (essay)

name: Mark Chen
bio: Mark Chen is chief research officer at OpenAI. He was lead author of the 2021 paper that introduced Codex, OpenAI's code model.

name: Mark Nitzberg
bio: Mark Nitzberg is executive director of the Center for Human-Compatible AI at UC Berkeley and head of strategic outreach for Berkeley AI Research.

name: Martin Wattenberg
role: Gordon McKay Professor of Computer Science
bio: Martin Wattenberg is a scientist and artist known for data visualization. He is a professor at Harvard and worked with Fernanda Viegas at IBM and Google.

name: Mausam
role: Professor of Computer Science and Engineering
bio: Mausam is a professor of computer science at IIT Delhi who works on natural language processing and AI.

name: Max Welling
bio: Max Welling is a Dutch machine learning researcher at the University of Amsterdam. He co-created variational autoencoders with Durk Kingma.

name: Michael I. Jordan
bio: Michael I. Jordan is a leading figure in machine learning and statistics at UC Berkeley. In 2016 Science called him the most influential computer scientist in the world.

name: Michael Wooldridge
bio: Michael Wooldridge is a professor of computer science at Oxford who studies multi-agent systems. He uses logic and game theory to study how AI agents act together.

name: Michaël Trazzi
bio: Michaël Trazzi hosts The Inside View, a podcast and YouTube channel of long interviews with AI alignment researchers. He also makes documentary work about AI risk and has campaigned publicly for slowing frontier AI.
key_ideas: Host of The Inside View podcast
Interviews with Collin Burns, Rob Miles, Ethan Perez and many others
Public campaigning on AI risk (2025 hunger strike outside Google DeepMind)

name: Mike Krieger
bio: Mike Krieger is a Brazilian-born co-founder of Instagram. He joined Anthropic in 2024 as chief product officer.

name: Mira Murati
bio: Mira Murati is the co-founder and CEO of Thinking Machines Lab, which she launched in 2025. She was chief technology officer of OpenAI from 2022 to 2024.

name: Nando de Freitas
bio: Nando de Freitas is a Zimbabwe-born machine learning researcher known for deep learning and Bayesian optimization. He led generative audio and image work at DeepMind.

name: Nicolas Papernot
bio: Nicolas Papernot works on security, privacy and machine learning at the University of Toronto. He co-directs the Canadian AI Safety Institute Research Program at CIFAR.

quotes.text: Although many philosophers used to dismiss the relevance of neuroscience on grounds that what mattered was “the software, not the hardware”, increasingly philosophers have come to recognize that understanding how the brain works is essential to understanding the mind.
quotes.source: Homepage, University of California, San Diego (via Wikiquote)

name: Patricia Churchland
bio: Patricia Churchland founded neurophilosophy with her 1986 book of that name, insisting that you cannot understand the mind without understanding the brain. She rejects the old view that only 'the software, not the hardware' matters, which also makes her cautious about assuming that today's AI thinks the way brains do. Her later work traces morality and conscience to evolved brain systems for caring and social bonding. She has spoken about the power and limits of artificial intelligence, stressing how much of real intelligence depends on biology.
key_ideas: Neurophilosophy: the mind is what the brain does
Morality rooted in evolved caring circuits
Limits of AI compared to biological brains

name: Paul Riechers
bio: Paul Riechers is a researcher at Simplex, an AI safety group building a theory of how neural networks organize their internal representations.

name: Pieter Abbeel
bio: Pieter Abbeel is a robotics and deep reinforcement learning researcher at UC Berkeley. He co-directs the Berkeley AI Research lab and co-founded Covariant.

name: Ponnurangam Kumaraguru
bio: Ponnurangam Kumaraguru is a professor at IIIT Hyderabad who leads the Precog research group. His work spans online safety, security and safe AI.

name: Q. Vera Liao
bio: Q. Vera Liao studies human-AI interaction at the University of Michigan. Her work looks at AI transparency and how it affects trust, reliance, control and oversight.

name: Raja Chatila
role: Professor of Robotics, AI and Ethics
bio: Raja Chatila is a French professor of robotics, AI and ethics at Sorbonne University. He led the Institute of Intelligent Systems and Robotics from 2014 to 2019.

name: Ricardo Baeza-Yates
bio: Ricardo Baeza-Yates is a Chilean computer scientist who works on web search and responsible AI. He is an expert member of the Global Partnership on AI.

name: Richard S. Sutton
bio: Richard Sutton is one of the founders of modern reinforcement learning. He won the 2024 Turing Award with Andrew Barto and wrote the essay The Bitter Lesson.

name: Robert Trager
bio: Robert Trager is co-director of the Oxford Martin AI Governance Initiative, which works on frontier and international AI governance.

name: Roger Grosse
bio: Roger Grosse is an associate professor at the University of Toronto and a founding member of the Vector Institute. He also works on the Alignment Science team at Anthropic.
warning: He says AI is moving so fast that making sure AIs stay robustly aligned with human values is urgent.

name: Rumman Chowdhury
bio: Rumman Chowdhury is a data scientist who works on responsible AI. She led responsible AI at Accenture and the machine learning ethics team at Twitter.

name: Seth Lazar
bio: Seth Lazar is a British philosopher who leads the Machine Intelligence and Normative Theory Lab. He studies the morality, law and politics of AI.

name: Shahar Avin
org: Leverhulme Centre for the Future of Intelligence, Cambridge
bio: Shahar Avin is a senior research associate at the Leverhulme Centre for the Future of Intelligence in Cambridge. He co-authored the 2018 report on the malicious use of AI.

name: Shakir Mohamed
bio: Shakir Mohamed is a research director at Google DeepMind who works on generative AI, weather and climate, and sociotechnical AI. He works for African AI leadership and safety.

name: Sheila McIlraith
bio: Sheila McIlraith is a Canadian AI researcher at the University of Toronto and the Vector Institute. She studies sequential decision-making with a focus on human-compatible AI.

name: Simon Chesterman
bio: Simon Chesterman is an Australian legal scholar at the National University of Singapore who studies how to regulate AI. He was senior director of AI governance at AI Singapore.
books: We, the Robots? Regulating Artificial Intelligence and the Limits of the Law

name: Stella Biderman
bio: Stella Biderman is the executive director of EleutherAI. She studies how large models gain abilities, how to make open-weight models safer, and how outside researchers can shape AI.

name: Thomas Wolf
bio: Thomas Wolf is a co-founder of Hugging Face, the open platform for AI models. He led the Transformers library paper.
warning: He signed Pacing the Frontier, saying AI progress has already outpaced society's ability to handle it.

quotes.text: AI progress has already out-paced society’s capabilities to handle it, let’s be careful for it not to out-pace its builder’s capabilities to control it. The journey is as important as the destination.
quotes.source: Pacing the Frontier, signatory comment

name: Virginia Dignum
bio: Virginia Dignum is a Dutch-Portuguese AI researcher who leads the Responsible AI group and the AI Policy Lab at Umea University in Sweden. In 2023 she joined the UN Secretary-General's AI Advisory Body.

name: Vukosi Marivate
bio: Vukosi Marivate is a South African computer scientist at the University of Pretoria. He co-founded the Deep Learning Indaba, Masakhane and Lelapa AI, and works on language AI for African languages.

name: Wojciech Zaremba
bio: Wojciech Zaremba is a Polish computer scientist and a co-founder of OpenAI. He led its robotics work and later teams on GPT models, Codex and GitHub Copilot.

name: Xue Lan
bio: Xue Lan is a Chinese public policy scholar at Tsinghua University. He directs its Institute for AI International Governance and China's National Expert Committee on Next Generation AI governance.

name: Yutaka Matsuo
bio: Yutaka Matsuo is a professor at the University of Tokyo who works on AI and web engineering. His lab is known for training students who start AI companies.

name: Zeng Yi
bio: Zeng Yi is a Chinese AI ethics and brain-inspired AI researcher. He works on AI ethics principles and cross-cultural cooperation on AI governance.

name: Zhang Ya-Qin
role: Founding Dean, Institute for AI Industry Research
bio: Zhang Ya-Qin is a Chinese scientist and business leader. He was president of Baidu and is now founding dean of Tsinghua's Institute for AI Industry Research.

name: Zhou Bowen
bio: Zhou Bowen is a Chinese computer scientist who leads the Shanghai AI Laboratory. His research covers AGI, large language models, AI safety and alignment.

name: Adam Shai
bio: Adam Shai is a researcher at Simplex, which studies the latent structure inside neural networks as a path to AI safety.

name: Alexander Meinke
bio: Alexander Meinke is a research scientist at Apollo Research. He was lead author of 'Frontier Models are Capable of In-context Scheming', which showed models deceiving users in test settings.
key_ideas: Lead author of the in-context scheming paper

name: Aza Raskin
bio: Aza Raskin is a co-founder of the Center for Humane Technology and the Earth Species Project. He co-hosts the podcast Your Undivided Attention.

name: Been Kim
bio: Been Kim leads interpretability work at Google DeepMind. She wants humans to stay in charge by learning useful knowledge from AI, for example teaching chess grandmasters ideas from AlphaZero.

name: Ben Buchanan
bio: Ben Buchanan is a consultant for Anthropic.

name: Greg Brockman
bio: Greg Brockman is a co-founder and the president of OpenAI. He was the first CTO of Stripe.

quotes.text: A robot may not injure a human being or, through inaction, allow a human being to come to harm.
quotes.source: First Law of Robotics, "Runaround" (1942), collected in I, Robot (1950)

name: Isaac Asimov
bio: Isaac Asimov was one of the most widely read science-fiction writers of the 20th century. His Three Laws of Robotics, first set out in the 1942 story "Runaround", were an early attempt to imagine built-in rules that keep machines safe for people. Many of his stories show those rules failing in unexpected ways, which is why AI-safety researchers still use them to explain why simple rules are not enough. He also wrote and spoke widely about computers and the future.
key_ideas: rule-based machine safety and its loopholes
stance: imagined rules to keep robots safe

name: Jade Leung
bio: Jade Leung is an engineer and AI governance leader. She was chief technology officer of the UK AI Security Institute and is now its vice chair.

name: Jakub Pachocki
bio: Jakub Pachocki is a Polish computer scientist and the chief scientist of OpenAI. He led work on GPT-4.
warning: In September 2026 he wrote that no AI company has solved alignment well enough to keep scaling at full speed for much longer.

quotes.text: solved alignment and monitoring to a sufficient degree to continue responsibly scaling at maximum speed for much longer
quotes.source: Blog post, as quoted by CNBC

quotes.text: I expect and hope for voluntary slowdowns to become commonplace until shared safety bars are established
quotes.source: Blog post, as quoted by CNBC

name: Lucas Perry
bio: Lucas Perry hosted the Future of Life Institute Podcast and its AI Alignment Podcast series. He interviewed dozens of alignment researchers about their agendas between 2018 and 2022.
key_ideas: Hosted the FLI AI Alignment Podcast
Long interviews with Evan Hubinger, Rohin Shah, Stuart Russell and others
Worked on existential risk outreach at FLI

name: Meredith Ringel Morris
bio: Meredith Ringel Morris works where human-computer interaction meets AI. She is a principal scientist and director at Google DeepMind and an affiliate professor at the University of Washington.

name: Stephanie Chan
bio: Stephanie Chan is a staff research scientist at Google DeepMind who has worked in AI for a decade.
warning: She signed Pacing the Frontier, warning that AI may progress far faster than societies and states can adapt.

quotes.text: Thus, many prominent leaders in AI have publicly supported the ability to slow down, including DeepMind CEO Demis Hassabis. At the same time, coordination is hampered by multiple factors, including competitive dynamics and antitrust regulations.
quotes.source: Pacing the Frontier, signatory comment

name: Tamay Besiroglu
org: Mechanize (acquired by Google in 2026); Epoch AI co-founder
bio: Tamay Besiroglu co-founded Epoch AI and later the automation startup Mechanize, which Google acquired in 2026. He researches the economics of AI and argues for long AGI timelines.

name: Tim Scarfe
bio: Tim Scarfe hosts Machine Learning Street Talk (MLST), a technical podcast with long interviews and debates on AI research and safety.
key_ideas: Host of Machine Learning Street Talk
Hosted debates on AI alignment and risk

name: Tom McGrath
bio: Tom McGrath is co-founder and chief scientist of Goodfire, an interpretability company. He previously did interpretability research at Google DeepMind, including on AlphaZero's chess knowledge.

name: Tomek Korbak
org: Formerly UK AI Security Institute and OpenAI
bio: Tomek Korbak works on AI control, safety cases and chain-of-thought monitorability, previously at the UK AI Security Institute and OpenAI. In 2026 he was fired from OpenAI along with Mikita Balesni and spoke publicly about it.

name: Vitalik Buterin
bio: Vitalik Buterin co-founded Ethereum. His 2023 essay on 'd/acc' argues for speeding up defensive and decentralized technology while being careful about AI.
warning: Technology is amazing, but AI is different and we should be uniquely careful.

quotes.text: AI is fundamentally different from other tech, and it is worth being uniquely careful
quotes.source: My techno-optimism (blog)

name: Abhishek Singh
org: Ministry of Electronics and IT, India
bio: Abhishek Singh is an Additional Secretary at India's Ministry of Electronics and IT and CEO of the IndiaAI Mission, which set up the IndiaAI Safety Institute in 2025.

name: Adrià Garriga-Alonso
bio: Adrià Garriga-Alonso is a research scientist at FAR.AI working on interpretability, including finding planning inside neural networks. He has also written publicly about why alignment might happen by default.
key_ideas: Interpretability of planning in game-playing networks
Work on detecting AI scheming via internal planning
Essay 'Alignment will happen by default; what's next?'

name: Amanda Askell
bio: Amanda Askell is a Scottish philosopher who leads the team that shapes Claude's character and constitution at Anthropic. She was on the TIME 100 AI list in 2024.

name: Arthur Conmy
bio: Arthur Conmy is an AI researcher in London who did early work in mechanistic interpretability. After Google DeepMind from 2023 to 2026, he joined Anthropic to align models as they are trained.

name: Brian Tse
bio: Brian Tse is the founder and CEO of Concordia AI, a Beijing-based social enterprise focused on AI safety and governance. He is also a policy affiliate at GovAI.

name: Daniel Ziegler
bio: Daniel Ziegler is a former OpenAI researcher who worked on learning from human preferences. He signed the 2024 Right to Warn letter.
warning: He says workers are among the few who can hold AI companies to account, but broad secrecy deals stop them from speaking.

quotes.text: So long as there is no effective government oversight of these corporations, current and former employees are among the few people who can hold them accountable to the public.
quotes.source: A Right to Warn about Advanced Artificial Intelligence (co-signer)

name: David Bau
bio: David Bau studies the inner structure of deep networks at Northeastern University.

name: Ege Erdil
bio: Ege Erdil was a researcher at Epoch AI, where he co-developed the GATE model of AI and the economy, before co-founding Mechanize. He is known for contrarian, long-timeline views.

name: George Hotz
bio: George Hotz is a hacker and entrepreneur who founded comma.ai and tiny corp. In AI safety he appears mainly as a sceptical debater, arguing against fast AI takeover scenarios.
key_ideas: First to jailbreak the iPhone; founder of comma.ai (self-driving) and tiny corp
Public debates with Eliezer Yudkowsky and Connor Leahy on AI risk

name: Hannah Fry
bio: Hannah Fry is a mathematician, author and broadcaster who hosts Google DeepMind: The Podcast. She interviews DeepMind researchers in plain language for general audiences.
key_ideas: Host of Google DeepMind: The Podcast
Author of "Hello World" on algorithms in society

name: Jeremie Harris
bio: Jeremie Harris is co-founder and CEO of Gladstone AI, which wrote a 2024 US State Department-commissioned report on catastrophic AI risk. He earlier hosted the Towards Data Science podcast, interviewing many alignment researchers.
key_ideas: Co-author of the Gladstone AI action plan on AI national security risks (2024)
Hosted the Towards Data Science podcast
Co-hosts the Last Week in AI podcast

name: Joshua Achiam
bio: Joshua Achiam is a researcher at OpenAI and an author of the GPT-4 technical report.
warning: He signed Pacing the Frontier, saying many frontier AI capabilities are dual use in a way that may justify pacing now.

quotes.text: government should develop increased capacity to understand and possibly pace, but this is worth serious consideration; however I hope such governance tools will not be expansive or excessive. But many frontier AI capabilities are dual use in a way that may justify pacing at this point.
quotes.source: Pacing the Frontier, signatory comment

name: Lawrence Chan
org: California Governor's Office of Emergency Services
bio: Lawrence Chan is the AI science advisor to California's Office of Emergency Services. Before that he evaluated frontier AI models at METR and co-led research on the time horizon of AI agents.

name: Lee Sharkey
bio: Lee Sharkey is an interpretability researcher at Goodfire and a co-founder of Apollo Research. He developed parameter decomposition methods and led the 'Open Problems in Mechanistic Interpretability' review.

name: Mikita Balesni
bio: Mikita Balesni was a founding research scientist at Apollo Research and co-discovered the 'Reversal Curse' with Owain Evans. In 2026 he was fired from OpenAI along with Tomek Korbak and spoke publicly about it.

name: Ross Girshick
bio: Ross Girshick is a computer vision researcher at Anthropic. He created R-CNN and co-authored Faster R-CNN and Mask R-CNN.

name: Sarah Schwettmann
bio: Sarah Schwettmann is a co-founder and the chief scientist of Transluce, a nonprofit lab building open tools for public oversight of AI systems.

name: Trenton Bricken
bio: Trenton Bricken works on the Alignment Science team at Anthropic, building ways for Claude to audit models and detect misalignment.

name: Christina Montgomery
bio: Christina Montgomery was IBM's Chief Privacy and Trust Officer and chaired its AI Ethics Board. She testified with Sam Altman and Gary Marcus at the May 2023 US Senate hearing on AI oversight.
key_ideas: Testified at the US Senate Judiciary hearing on AI oversight (May 16, 2023)
Argued for "precision regulation" of AI by use case

name: Collin Burns
bio: Collin Burns is an AI researcher who worked at OpenAI and Anthropic. He led work on weak-to-strong generalization and on finding latent knowledge in language models.

name: David Rein
bio: David Rein is a researcher at METR and co-author of its time-horizon paper. He was earlier lead author of the GPQA benchmark of graduate-level science questions.
key_ideas: Lead author of the GPQA benchmark
Explaining what capability trends do and don't show

name: Fabien Roger
bio: Fabien Roger is an AI safety researcher who worked at Redwood Research on AI control and capability elicitation before joining Anthropic. He co-authored the original AI control paper.
key_ideas: Co-author of 'AI Control: Improving Safety Despite Intentional Subversion'
Core contributor to 'Alignment faking in large language models'
Research on eliciting capabilities from scheming models

name: Gregory Wayne
bio: Gregory Wayne is a distinguished scientist at Google DeepMind. He co-authored Neural Turing Machines.

name: Ian Hogarth
role: Investor, former Chair of the UK AI Safety Institute
org: UK AI Security Institute (formerly Frontier AI Taskforce)
bio: Ian Hogarth is a tech investor who chaired the UK government's Frontier AI Taskforce, which became the AI Safety Institute. He co-founded Songkick and Plural Platform.
warning: Governments need their own expert capacity to test and understand frontier AI.

quotes.text: UK scientists and entrepreneurs have made many important contributions to the field of AI, from Alan Turing through to AlphaFold.
quotes.source: UK government announcement of his appointment

name: Jan Kirchner
bio: Jan Hendrik Kirchner is an alignment researcher at Anthropic working on scalable oversight. At OpenAI's Superalignment team he co-authored weak-to-strong generalization and prover-verifier games.
key_ideas: Lead author of prover-verifier games for legibility
PhD in computational neuroscience (Max Planck Institute)

name: Joshua Batson
bio: Joshua Batson is an interpretability researcher at Anthropic who works on tracing the internal circuits of language models.

name: Julian Schrittwieser
bio: Julian Schrittwieser is a researcher at Anthropic. At DeepMind he was first author of MuZero and worked on AlphaGo and AlphaProof.

name: Jérémy Scheurer
bio: Jérémy Scheurer is a research scientist at Apollo Research working on reinforcement learning, evaluations and scheming. He co-authored 'Open problems and fundamental limitations of RLHF' and the in-context scheming paper.
key_ideas: Co-author of the in-context scheming paper
Co-author of 'Open problems and limitations of RLHF'

name: Kaiming He
bio: Kaiming He is a computer vision researcher and one of the creators of ResNet. His 2016 ResNet paper is one of the most cited papers in all of science.

name: Li-Lian Ang
bio: Li-Lian Ang works at BlueDot Impact and writes guides for people starting out in AI safety. Her posts help learners decide which course fits them.
warning: Anyone who cares about the future and is ready to act can start learning AI safety.

quotes.text: We’ve designed these courses for driven individuals determined to make a real difference.
quotes.source: Am I the right fit for BlueDot's courses? (BlueDot blog)

quotes.text: Our courses are tailored for those who recognise the potential risks of emerging technologies and are motivated to take action to ensure they are used to benefit humanity positively.
quotes.source: Am I the right fit for BlueDot's courses? (BlueDot blog)

name: Lionel Levine
bio: Lionel Levine is a Cornell mathematician known for work on sandpiles and abelian networks who has moved into AI safety. He speaks about what mathematicians can contribute to safety and about cooperation among AI agents.
key_ideas: Research on abelian sandpiles and random walks
'Math for AI Safety' talks inviting mathematicians into the field
Work on 'inherent kindness' and multi-agent safety in RL

name: Luisa Rodriguez
bio: Luisa Rodriguez is a host of The 80,000 Hours Podcast and a researcher on global catastrophic risks.
key_ideas: Research on civilisational collapse and recovery
Interviews on AI governance and compute

name: Margaret Mitchell
bio: Margaret Mitchell studies bias and fairness in machine learning. She is known for model cards, a way to report what a model is for.

name: Samuel Marks
bio: Samuel Marks is a researcher at Anthropic who works on interpretability and alignment auditing.

name: Sayash Kapoor
bio: Sayash Kapoor is a Princeton researcher who co-wrote AI Snake Oil and 'AI as Normal Technology' with Arvind Narayanan. He studies how AI claims hold up in the real world.
warning: We should treat AI as a powerful but normal technology and focus on how society adopts it.

quotes.text: AI as normal technology is a worldview that stands in contrast to the worldview of AI as impending superintelligence.
quotes.source: AI as Normal Technology (with Arvind Narayanan)

name: Simon Lermen
bio: Simon Lermen is an AI safety researcher whose work shows how cheaply safety training can be removed from open-weight models. He has also studied AI agents used for spear-phishing.
key_ideas: Showed LoRA fine-tuning can undo safety training in Llama 2-Chat (2023)
Writes on AI risk on his Substack

name: Spencer Greenberg
bio: Spencer Greenberg is a mathematician and entrepreneur who founded ClearerThinking.org and hosts the Clearer Thinking podcast.
key_ideas: Founder of ClearerThinking.org and Spark Wave
Host of the Clearer Thinking podcast
Conversations on rationality and AI risk

name: Zershaaneh Qureshi
bio: Zershaaneh Qureshi is a host on The 80,000 Hours Podcast, interviewing researchers about AI safety.
key_ideas: Interview with Owain Evans on emergent misalignment

name: Akbir Khan
bio: Akbir Khan is an AI safety researcher who works on scalable oversight. He was lead author of a 2024 ICML best-paper study showing that debating with more persuasive AI models helps humans reach truer answers.
key_ideas: Lead author of "Debating with More Persuasive LLMs Leads to More Truthful Answers" (ICML 2024 best paper)
Research on debate as a scalable oversight method
PhD work at University College London

name: Andrew Yao
role: Dean, Institute for Interdisciplinary Information Sciences
bio: Andrew Yao is a computer scientist who won the 2000 Turing Award. He leads the Institute for Interdisciplinary Information Sciences at Tsinghua University.
warning: In 2024 he joined Bengio, Hinton and others in a paper warning that AI safety research is falling behind and that extreme risks need governance now.

name: Axel Højmark
bio: Axel Højmark is a researcher at Apollo Research, which evaluates AI systems for scheming and deception. He discusses how Apollo tests models for hidden goals.
key_ideas: Evaluations for scheming at Apollo Research
Discussed testing AI for hidden goals on Machine Learning Street Talk

name: Benjamin Wright
bio: Benjamin Wright is an alignment researcher at Anthropic. He co-authored the alignment-faking study and later work on emergent misalignment from reward hacking.
key_ideas: Co-author of "Alignment faking in large language models" (2024)
Co-author of research on natural emergent misalignment from reward hacking (2025)
Works on model organisms of misalignment

name: Beren Millidge
bio: Beren Millidge is an AI researcher who works on predictive coding, alignment and AI capabilities. He was previously head of research at Conjecture.
key_ideas: Research on predictive coding and its links to backpropagation
Former head of research at Conjecture
Writes on alignment and AI progress

name: Bowen Baker
bio: Bowen Baker is a research scientist at OpenAI. He led work on monitoring the chain-of-thought of reasoning models for misbehaviour and earlier on emergent tool use in multi-agent hide-and-seek.
key_ideas: Lead author of "Monitoring Reasoning Models for Misbehavior" (2025) on chain-of-thought monitoring
Co-author of the cross-lab position paper on chain-of-thought monitorability
Led OpenAI's emergent tool use "hide-and-seek" project (2019)

name: Bronson Schoen
bio: Bronson Schoen is a researcher at Apollo Research. He was lead author of the 2025 study with OpenAI on training models not to scheme.
key_ideas: Lead author of the Apollo Research and OpenAI anti-scheming study (2025)
Research on evaluation awareness in frontier models

name: Charlie O'Neill
bio: Charlie O'Neill is a machine-learning researcher. He joined a 2026 Dwarkesh Patel panel debating how close AI is to recursive self-improvement.
key_ideas: Panellist in Dwarkesh Patel's recursive self-improvement debate (2026)

name: Gus Docker
bio: Gus Docker hosts the Future of Life Institute Podcast, interviewing researchers about AI risk, governance and alignment.
key_ideas: Host of the Future of Life Institute Podcast
Interviews on AI risk, governance and alignment

name: Jerry Wei
bio: Jerry Wei is a research scientist at Anthropic who works on safeguards against misuse. He co-authored Anthropic's Constitutional Classifiers work on defending models against universal jailbreaks.
key_ideas: Co-author of "Constitutional Classifiers" (2025) against universal jailbreaks
Earlier research at Google DeepMind on long-form factuality and sycophancy

name: Jess Whittlestone
bio: Jess Whittlestone is senior advisor on AI policy at the Centre for Long-Term Resilience, a UK think tank on extreme risks.

name: Joe Benton
bio: Joe Benton managed Anthropic's Scalable Oversight team and worked on control evaluations, chain-of-thought monitoring and sabotage evaluations. He left Anthropic for METR in September 2026.
key_ideas: Co-author of 'Sabotage Evaluations for Frontier Models'
Designed AI control evaluations for Anthropic's RSP

name: Laura Weidinger
bio: Laura Weidinger is a staff research scientist at Google DeepMind who studies the ethical and social risks of language models.
warning: She signed Pacing the Frontier, warning that a mindless race without safety and governance stands in the way of introducing AI with care.

quotes.text: A mindless race without assurances on governance, safety or the technology serving the public interest stands in the way of such intentionality.
quotes.source: Pacing the Frontier, signatory comment

name: Lawrence Lessig
bio: Lawrence Lessig is a legal scholar at Harvard Law School and the founder of Creative Commons. He gave free legal help to AI workers who want to warn the public.

name: Leo Gao
bio: Leo Gao is a researcher at OpenAI who writes about AI alignment and scaling language models. He co-authored OpenAI's weak-to-strong generalization work.
warning: He signed Pacing the Frontier and warns the world is in a deadly race toward an intelligence explosion.

quotes.text: The world is locked in a deadly race towards an intelligence explosion, where AI’s ability to create better AIs reaches a critical point, just like a runaway nuclear chain reaction. Going slower would give us much-needed time to make it go well, but no individual actor is willing to stop unilaterally.
quotes.source: Pacing the Frontier, signatory comment

name: Marietje Schaake
bio: Marietje Schaake is a Dutch former member of the European Parliament who now works on tech policy at Stanford. Politico called her the ultimate digital MEP.

name: Mark Xu
bio: Mark Xu is a researcher at the Alignment Research Center. He co-authored ARC's Eliciting Latent Knowledge report and the paper on formalizing the presumption of independence.

name: Mary Phuong
bio: Mary Phuong is a senior research scientist at Google DeepMind. She was first author of the 2024 paper on evaluating frontier models for dangerous capabilities.

name: Meg Tong
bio: Meg Tong is a researcher at Anthropic. She co-authored research on sycophancy in language models and on Constitutional Classifiers against jailbreaks.
key_ideas: Co-author of "Towards Understanding Sycophancy in Language Models" (2023)
Works on safeguards and alignment evaluations

name: Mia Glaese
bio: Mia Glaese is a researcher at OpenAI. At DeepMind she was first author of the Sparrow paper on making dialogue agents more helpful and harmless.

name: Monte MacDiarmid
bio: Monte MacDiarmid is an alignment researcher at Anthropic. He works on model organisms of misalignment, including the alignment-faking study and research on emergent misalignment from reward hacking.
key_ideas: Co-author of "Alignment faking in large language models" (2024)
Lead author of work on natural emergent misalignment from reward hacking (2025)
Co-author of "Simple probes can catch sleeper agents"

name: Mrinank Sharma
bio: Mrinank Sharma led Anthropic's Safeguards Research Team until early 2026. His work covers jailbreak defences, sycophancy and AI-assisted misuse.
key_ideas: Co-author of Constitutional Classifiers and "Towards Understanding Sycophancy in Language Models"
PhD in machine learning from the University of Oxford

name: Nicholas Carlini
bio: Nicholas Carlini is a security researcher known for showing how machine learning systems can be fooled. His Carlini and Wagner attack broke many early defenses.

name: Sam Marks
bio: Samuel Marks leads Anthropic's Cognitive Oversight team within Alignment Science. He is known for alignment auditing games and earlier interpretability work on the geometry of truth.
key_ideas: Lead author of 'Auditing Language Models for Hidden Objectives'
'The Geometry of Truth' and sparse feature circuits
Proposed the persona selection model of AI assistants

name: Scott Emmons
bio: Scott Emmons is an AI safety researcher who did his PhD at UC Berkeley's Center for Human-Compatible AI. His work studies how RLHF can fail under partial observability, letting models deceive their evaluators.
key_ideas: Research on RLHF failures under partial observability (deception and overjustification)
Works on chain-of-thought monitoring and evaluations

name: Sebastian Farquhar
bio: Sebastian Farquhar is a staff research scientist at Google DeepMind, where he leads the Frontier Safety Loss of Control team. He is also a senior research fellow at OATML in Oxford.
warning: He says some changes from AGI could be catastrophically bad, and his main goal is to reduce that harm.

name: Summer Yue
bio: Summer Yue is director of alignment and risk at Meta.

name: Tejal Patwardhan
bio: Tejal Patwardhan is a researcher at OpenAI who led work on an early warning system for AI-aided biological threats.

name: Timnit Gebru
bio: Timnit Gebru is a computer scientist who studies bias in AI. She co-founded Black in AI and founded the DAIR Institute.
warning: She warns that large language models carry real harms now, like bias and cost, and that big companies silence critics.

name: Todor Markov
bio: Todor Markov worked at OpenAI from 2018, ending on the Preparedness team where he tested how persuasive AI models are. He now works at Anthropic.
warning: He says he left OpenAI because he lost trust in its leadership.

quotes.text: I left OpenAI in 2024 because I lost trust in its leadership team.
quotes.source: Declaration in Musk v. Altman amicus brief

name: Adly Templeton
bio: Adly Templeton is an interpretability researcher at Anthropic. He was first author of Scaling Monosemanticity, which found millions of features inside Claude 3 Sonnet.

name: Carroll Wainwright
bio: Carroll Wainwright is a former OpenAI researcher. He signed the 2024 Right to Warn letter and joined the 2025 amicus brief of former OpenAI staff.
warning: He says OpenAI acted like a for-profit, so its nonprofit promise to do the right thing turned out empty.

quotes.text: OpenAI was structured as a non-profit, but it acted like a for-profit.
quotes.source: Post on X, via The OpenAI Files

quotes.text: Now that the stakes are high, the non-profit structure is being abandoned, which means the promise was ultimately empty.
quotes.source: Post on X, via The OpenAI Files

name: Dewi Erwan
bio: Dewi Erwan co-founded BlueDot Impact, which runs free online courses in AI safety, AI governance and biosecurity. More than 10,000 people have taken BlueDot courses.
warning: The field desperately needs more capable people to own the hardest problems in AI safety.

quotes.text: We’re trying to build a world where decision-makers are equipped to ensure powerful new technologies benefit all of humanity.
quotes.source: 2023 Impact Report Summary (BlueDot Impact)

quotes.text: Building AI safety and biosecurity talent infrastructure is tractable, neglected and desperately needed.
quotes.source: What we're building at BlueDot (blog)

name: Gretchen Krueger
bio: Gretchen Krueger is a former policy researcher at OpenAI who quit in May 2024. She said she shared the safety concerns of Ilya Sutskever and Jan Leike.
warning: She says AI companies need better decision-making, accountability and transparency, and warns that companies can silence critics by dividing them.

quotes.text: I resigned a few hours before hearing the news about @ilyasut and @janleike, and I made my decision independently. I share their concerns. I also have additional and overlapping concerns.
quotes.source: Post on X, via Business Insider

quotes.text: One of the ways tech companies in general can disempower those seeking to hold them accountable is to sow division among those raising concerns or challenging their power.
quotes.source: Post on X, via Business Insider

name: Karel Čapek
bio: Karel Čapek was a Czech writer whose 1920 play R.U.R. (Rossum's Universal Robots) introduced the word "robot" to the world. In the play, artificial workers built to serve people eventually revolt and wipe out humanity. The story set the template for a century of fiction about created minds turning on their makers. It remains a reference point whenever people discuss AI control and machine labour.

name: Kim Myuhng-joo
bio: Kim Myuhng-joo is the first director of the Korea AI Safety Institute, which opened in November 2024. He is a security and digital ethics expert who wrote the book AI Has No Conscience.

quotes.text: The institute will play a role as an organization supporting local AI companies to minimize risk factors that can hinder the firms from strengthening their global competitiveness, rather than working as a regulatory body
quotes.source: Opening ceremony, via Yonhap

name: Saachi Jain
bio: Saachi Jain is head of safety at OpenAI.

quotes.text: the time will come when the machines will hold the real supremacy over the world and its inhabitants
quotes.source: "Darwin among the Machines", letter to The Press (Christchurch)

quotes.text: Our opinion is that war to the death should be instantly proclaimed against them.
quotes.source: "Darwin among the Machines", letter to The Press (Christchurch)

name: Samuel Butler
bio: Samuel Butler was a Victorian English writer who was among the first to argue that machines could evolve the way living things do. In his 1863 letter "Darwin among the Machines" he warned that machines were gaining ground on humanity and might one day rule it. He expanded the idea in his satirical novel Erewhon, whose citizens destroy their machines out of fear. His essay is often cited as the earliest written warning about machine takeover.

name: Shengjia Zhao
bio: Shengjia Zhao is chief scientist of Meta AI. Before that he was a researcher at OpenAI and an author on the GPT-4 technical report.
warning: He signed Pacing the Frontier, saying frontier labs are very close to AI that can beat the best people on almost every measure of intelligence.

quotes.text: AI is progressing at a rate that our society might not be ready for. Frontier labs are very close to AI that can exceed even the best people on almost every metric of intelligence.
quotes.source: Pacing the Frontier, signatory comment
